Simple queries—such as information on schemes, downloading forms, or understanding market prices are often resolved during the call itself. Soil sampling, testing, analysis and issue of soil test report to farmers along with crop specific recommendation of fertilizers based on soil test outcome has been a mandate of the Department of Agriculture. From the year -2012 onwards soil test reports were given in a comprehensive manner as Farmers Integrated Handbook. From the year 2014-2015 onwards Soil Health Card (SHC) scheme was introduced under National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture, a centrally sponsored scheme under which support for soil sampling, analysis and printing of soil health cards was given. Soil Health Card is a semi-permanent record with a validity period of three years. The Soil Health Card scheme has been merged with Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) from the year 2023-2024.

2. The main objective of issuing Soil Health Card is to promote Integrated Nutrient Management through judicious use of chemical fertilizers including secondary and micro nutrients in conjunction with organic manures, bio fertilizers for improving soil health and ultimately the crop productivity.

3. Tamil Nadu soils are low in Organic Carbon and Nitrogen content, medium in Phosphorus content, high in Potassium content. With respect to Micronutrients, they are deficient in Zinc and Copper, sufficient in Sulphur, Boron, Manganese and Iron. Understanding soil fertility and to practice judicious use of fertilizers by farmers in the field is essential to

maintain soil health.

In pursuit of higher production, there is a tendency among farmers to use fertilizers and pesticides over and above the actual requirement leading to depletion of soil health, particularly, reduced microbial activity in the soil. It is also an established fact that excess chemical usage is one of the causes for many pest and diseases. There is a need to adopt soil test based balanced use of fertilizers by integrating bio/organic fertilizers into agriculture for nutritional security of soil. There are many traditional practices like application of botanicals, organic manuring etc that have to be revisited and embraced in a large scale without compromising on the production.

Adult education helps adults who have not had the advantage of formal schooling to learn basic knowledge and skills essential for meeting day-to-day requirements of life. Non-formal and adult education aims to organise systematic and sustained learning activities to help an illiterate adult gain new forms of knowledge and life skills. The primary objective is to enable these individuals to gain confidence by providing them with a basic education that may help enhance their earning capacity.

extracts.text:
3. The Government after careful examination have decided to accept the proposal of the Engineer-in-Chief and Chief Engineer (General), Water Resources Department, Chennai and hereby accord administrative sanction for a sum of Rs.66,00,000/- (Rupees Sixty Six lakhs only) for the Procurement of 3 Nos. of Multi Utility Vehicle (at the rate of Rs.22,00,000/- per vehicle) for Inspection, Patrolling, Operation and Maintenance Activities of Contour Canal, Aliyar Feeder Canal, Aliyar Dam and Aliyar River Irrigation in Aliyar Sub Basin of Parambikulam Aliyar Project in Anaimalai Taluk of Coimbatore District under A1 component of World Bank funded TNIAM Project, as a special case relaxing the ceiling limit of Rs.17,92,638.85 per vehicle prescribed for purchase of vehicles under Light Motor Vehicle (LMV) Passenger Complete Built Unit (CBU) category.

4. The expenditure sanctioned at para 3 above shall be debited to the following head of account:-

“2701 Medium Irrigation — 80 General — 001-Direction and Administration — Externally Aided Projects — PE Strengthening of Institutes for Offices(O&M) under TNIAM Project Il- 321—Motor Vehicles- 01 — Purchase.”

(IFHRMS DPC :2701-80-001-PE-321 01)

5. Necessary Additional Funds of Rs. 66,00,000/- will be provided in RE/FMA 2024-2025. However, this expenditure shall be brought to the notice of the legislature by way of Specific Inclusion in the Supplementary Estimate 2024-25. Pending provision of such funds, the Engineer-in-Chief and Chief Engineer (General), Water Resources Department, Chennai is auhorised to incur the expenditure sanctioned in para 3 above. He is also directed to include the above item of expenditure while sending the budget proposal for RE/FMA 2024-25 and also send necessary draft Explanatory note for inclusion of the expenditure in the Supplementary Estimate 2024-2025 to Finance (Infra-II/BG-1) Department at an appropriate time without fail.

6. This order issues with the concurrence of the Finance Department vide its U.O. No. efile/2881/Finance(Infra-Il)Department/2024, dated 02.09.2024 and Additional Sanction Ledger No.0746(Seven hundred and forty six) (IFHRMS ASL No.2024090746).
